title.value: Real-time Monitoring for the Next Core-Collapse Supernova in JUNO
title.justification: The title is directly stated at the beginning of the document and reflects the focus of the research on monitoring core-collapse supernovae using the JUNO detector.
title.quote: Real-time Monitoring for the Next Core-Collapse Supernova in JUNO

analysis.description: This research paper discusses the implementation of a real-time monitoring system for the next core-collapse supernova using the JUNO detector. It elaborates on the system's capability to detect pre-supernova and supernova neutrinos, providing early alerts for multi-messenger astrophysical observations. The method aims to improve detection through prompt and online monitoring systems, ensuring comprehensive coverage of stellar progenitors.

type.justification: The paper presents empirical results obtained through simulations and testing of the monitoring system for detecting neutrinos. It evaluates the sensitivity and alert capabilities of the system under real-world-like conditions.
type.quote: The performance of the prompt monitor is evaluated with simulated SN neutrino events from both the Nakazato and Garching models.

name.justification: The study focuses on detecting neutrinos from core-collapse supernovae, a significant event in the field of astrophysics, particularly in understanding stellar evolution and explosive astrophysical phenomena.
name.quote: The core-collapse supernova (CCSN) is considered one of the most energetic astrophysical events in the universe.

name.justification: The paper involves the detection of neutrinos and their interactions, which are fundamental aspects of particle physics.
name.quote: The detection of pre-SN and SN neutrinos provides significant opportunities to study the physics of CCSN explosions and related neutrino properties.

name.justification: The research focuses on implementing real-time data acquisition and monitoring systems for detecting astrophysical events.
name.quote: We describe the concept of the real-time monitoring system in JUNO and present its sensitivity.
